method: Read-only final source review and byte comparison; no UI, native or browser suites rerun.

checks.detail: Run/build/snapshot/scene/visit ownership, visibility and availability guard source tickets; close, filtering, removed or changed records revoke them. Appends preserve unchanged animation/clip tickets while delivery changes revoke only that subscriber ticket.

canOpenSource is click admission, intentionally not a continuation guard during own-loading. Host navigation epoch, dirty/creating checks and app-runtime source/editor tokens protect the final read, editor writes and focus.

Reader derives animation and clip declarations from the frozen scene plan and recipients from exact binding/instance/object identity; query validates visits and timeline. UI passes animation.source, clip.source and delivery.origin.source separately without inventing a publisher or interpreting objectId as a script UUID.

Completion labels update text nodes in place; search value/selection and unchanged source buttons remain stable. Both starter String fields use the unchanged generic clip picker and require explicit insertion plus normal review/apply/save.
Completion view admits protocol7 only; state/event/audio/command host gates include7 and retain legacy1–6 behavior. Command clip details remain visible for6/7.

New starter checks all four ports plus valid Object, subscribes without changing playback, matches nullable completed clip, selects then plays next, and clears/revokes subscription on exit. No author schema or execution authority is added to draft creation.

legacyStarters.proof: Removing the single appended completion-starter line yields the entire HEAD engine/script-authoring.mjs byte-for-byte.

limitations: Static audit supplements the existing completed UI/native checks; it is not an additional browser or installed-app acceptance run.
Rendering and narrow-screen behavior remain covered by the separately recorded Chrome run, not inferred from this audit.
